key_insight: A sparse-sensor, machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction framework can rapidly tune airfoil wake synchronization while explicitly constraining lift fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster post-stall flow control for aerodynamic systems where quick wake-frequency adjustment is needed without inducing harmful unsteady loads.
method: Use three sparse sensors with nonlinear ML-based reconstruction to estimate wake state.
Derive time-varying phase and amplitude sensitivity fields to locate optimal actuation timing and spatial forcing.
Analytically compute an optimal forcing waveform, including an amplitude-penalized variant for reduced lift variability.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on multiple NACA airfoils at several post-stall angles of attack, and the amplitude-penalized forcing reduced lift coefficient fluctuation by about 20% versus the unpenalized optimal forcing while changing wake frequency faster than sinusoidal actuation.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate sparse-sensor reconstruction and learned sensitivity fields, so performance may degrade if the flow departs from the periodic vortex-shedding regime or sensors are noisy/misplaced.
paper_title: Machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction for fast synchronization of airfoil wakes with constrained fluctuations
